setupFlow.arucoPrintPrompt: Print the origin marker used for camera extrinsics, then measure the black square's edge precisely. The marker defines the tracking world's origin, axes, and scale, so a mismeasured edge rescales everything.
setupFlow.avatarLoadPrompt: Single-camera tracking drives an avatar rather than a raw skeleton, so pick the VRM model first. The avatar's own bone lengths are the scale of the front-camera mode, and its elbow hints seed the desk mode's body solver.
setupFlow.charucoPrintPrompt: Print the checkerboard used for camera intrinsics, then measure it. Print dialogs rescale pages silently, so measure a black square on the printed sheet rather than trusting these numbers.
setupFlow.charucoValidationWarning: Columns/rows need at least 2, and the square must be larger than the marker
setupFlow.confirmCancelPrompt: Cancel the project setup? This new project will be DELETED from disk, including any calibration completed so far, and the app returns to the main menu.
setupFlow.dualOverheadHint: Sees the desk and hands only.
setupFlow.dualOverheadJoyConsHint: Sees the desk and hands; the Joy-Cons provide elbow pose.
setupFlow.handednessPrompt: Hold both hands up in view of the camera, apart from each other. This checks that the hand tracker's left and right match your body, and switches the Flip handedness setting if they do not.
setupFlow.handednessSwapped: The hand tracker's left and right labels are still reversed. The body model is correcting them while it sees the hands. Change Flip handedness in the tracking settings after setup.
setupFlow.handednessSwitched: Left and right were swapped: Flip handedness was switched to match this camera
setupFlow.handednessWaiting: Waiting for hands: hold both hands up with your wrists in frame
setupFlow.neutralPrompt: Sit as you will while streaming: facing the camera, head level. The capture zeroes the torso and the head to this pose. The hands need no capture. Set the camera tilt slider to the camera's downward angle: 10 for a webcam on top of the monitor, 0 at eye level, negative below the screen.
setupFlow.neutralTrackingWaiting: Waiting for tracking: sit in view of the camera with your shoulders in frame
setupFlow.pairingHint: Pair Joy-Cons in Windows Bluetooth settings; they connect here automatically once paired.
setupFlow.pickCameraPrompt: Pick a device for each camera.
setupFlow.singleDeskHint: One camera above or beside the desk that sees the marker; the avatar carries the output.
setupFlow.singleFrontHint: A webcam facing you from the monitor drives the avatar directly; no marker, no desk in view.
setupFlow.trackingSetupPrompt: What is your desired tracking setup?
setupFlow.triCameraFrontHint: Overhead cameras for hands; the front camera adds head and upper body.
setupFlow.triCameraFrontRadio: Two overhead cameras + one front camera

avatarPanel.armLengthsFmt: Arm: avatar %.0f + %.0f cm, you %.0f + %.0f cm (upper + forearm)
avatarPanel.elbowWeightTooltip:
How far the bend follows the measured elbow rather than the hint:
at 1 the measured elbow alone decides the bend, at 0 the hint alone.
The default function follows the forearm's confidence.
avatarPanel.elbowHintTooltip:
The point the elbow bends toward when the forearm is not measured:
meters from the shoulder in the avatar's torso frame
(+X forward, +Y the avatar's left, +Z up).
avatarPanel.restElbowTooltip: Where the elbow rests when the arm's tracking is lost: meters from the shoulder joint, +X forward, +Y the avatar's left, +Z up. Only the direction is used.
avatarPanel.restWristTooltip: Where the wrist rests, meters from the shoulder joint in the same frame. Only the direction from the rest elbow is used.
avatarPanel.restPalmTooltip: The direction the palm faces at rest, same frame. Straight down lays it on a desk.
avatarPanel.restCurlTooltip: How far the fingers curl at rest, degrees on the base and middle joints.
avatarPanel.restBlendTooltip: How long the chain takes to ease into its rest pose once its hold ends, milliseconds. Zero snaps.
avatarPanel.fixedRootHeader: Fixed placement (used while the shoulders are not tracked)
avatarPanel.followShouldersTooltip:
When the body-pose stage tracks both shoulders, the avatar
slides so its shoulders sit on the measured ones.
avatarPanel.frameTrimTooltip: Rotates the rest frame the measurement is matched to, in that frame's own axes (X, Y, Z degrees)
avatarPanel.leftHandIncompleteText: Left hand lacks finger bones; its fingers will not be retargeted
avatarPanel.mappingHelpText: Click a dot or a row to select a bone, then pick the node that plays it. Orange marks a suspect mapping, red a required bone without a node. The rotation trims are on the head, hand and arm chains.
avatarPanel.overriddenTooltipFmt: Overridden. The file maps this bone to %s
avatarPanel.previewPoseTooltip:
Rest and Demo pose the 3D scene's avatar from a canned frame,
so the rig can be tuned without cameras.
The VMC output always follows live tracking.
avatarPanel.requiredUnmapTooltip: Every VRM must map this bone, so it cannot be unmapped
avatarPanel.rightHandIncompleteText: Right hand lacks finger bones; its fingers will not be retargeted
avatarPanel.rollTrimTooltip: Adds a roll about the forearm, degrees
avatarPanel.shoulderWidthFmt: Shoulder width: avatar %.0f cm, you %.0f cm
avatarPanel.thumbPronationTooltip:
The twist of the thumb's bending axis. Automatic reads its direction
from the hand's bones; set it by hand when the thumb curls outward.

chains.afterEaseTooltip:
The avatar eases the chain from its last pose into its rest pose over the rest blend,
and keeps it there until it is tracked again. Its bones keep streaming, so a receiver
sees the same ease and then a still rest pose.
chains.afterFreezeTooltip:
The avatar keeps the chain in the last pose it was given until it is tracked again.
Its bones keep streaming unchanged, so a receiver sees the chain stop moving.
chains.afterReleaseTooltip:
The chain's bones are left out of the pose: the avatar shows them at its own rest,
and they stop streaming, so a receiver returns them to the avatar's rest pose
(the T-pose, for an arm).
chains.boneAnglesNote: The avatar's bones take your bones' directions, and its wrist lands where its own lengths put it.
chains.mirrorToOtherArmTooltip:
Copies this arm onto the other one, mirrored: the elbow hint, the measured
elbow weight, the reach scale, the goal offset, the forearm roll trim,
the loss policy, the rest pose, and the stored mapping and IK weight.
A function reads the other side. Points and directions reflect across the
body's midline, and the roll trim changes sign. The hand's settings are not copied.
chains.directArmLossNote: The arm holds for as long as its tracking has earned, up to half a second.
chains.easeWithoutAvatarNote: Without an avatar the stream has no rest pose, so the arm freezes instead.
chains.effectiveIkWeightTooltip:
The IK weight the arm was solved at on the shown frame: 0 for bone angles,
the IK weight for bone angles then IK. On a multi-camera project it moves to 1
while the arm's shoulder or elbow is not measured.
chains.goalOffsetTooltip:
Moves the IK goal of the wrist, meters, before the goal is clamped to the avatar's reach.
In the avatar's torso frame (+X forward, +Y the avatar's left, +Z up), so it turns with the avatar.
chains.handLossNote: A lost hand follows its arm's loss policy.
chains.headDirectLossNote: When its tracking is lost, the solver holds the head for up to half a second.
chains.headHoldTooltip:
After the head goes untracked, keep its last pose for this long
before what follows the hold (Then) applies. 0 = apply it immediately.
chains.headLimitTooltip:
The largest rotation the head takes away from the neutral head, degrees, from the phone or the camera alike.
A larger turn is clamped onto its own axis at this angle.
180 changes nothing, zero holds the head at the neutral pose. The head trim applies after it.
chains.ikWeightTooltip:
How far the wrist is pulled from where the bone angles put it toward the goal.
At 1 the arm reaches the goal (the IK alone), at 0 it keeps the bone angles.
On a multi-camera project an arm whose shoulder or elbow is not measured cannot take
the bone angles and takes the IK.
chains.mappingBoneAnglesThenIk: Bone angles, then IK to a goal
chains.mappingBoneAnglesThenIkTooltip:
The bone angles first, then the wrist is pulled toward a goal by the IK weight.
The goal is your reach from the shoulder placed on the avatar's shoulder,
scaled by the reach scale and moved by the goal offset.
chains.mappingBoneAnglesTooltip:
The avatar's upper arm and forearm take the directions of your upper arm and forearm.
Its wrist lands where its own bone lengths put it.
chains.reachScaleDirectTooltip:
How the measured reach from the shoulder to the wrist maps onto the avatar's arm.
At 1 it is scaled by the avatar's arm length over yours, so a full reach is a full reach.
At 0 it is kept as measured: your proportions at the avatar's shoulder width.
chains.reachScaleTooltip:
How the measured reach from the shoulder to the wrist maps onto the avatar's arm.
At 1 it is scaled by the avatar's arm length over yours, so a full reach is a full reach.
At 0 it is kept in meters, so the wrist goes where yours is and a shorter arm cannot reach as far.
chains.resetArmTooltip:
Resets the elbow hint, the measured elbow weight, the reach scale, the goal offset
and the rest pose, and the mapping and the IK weight to the project's defaults
(bone angles for a direct project, IK at 1 for a multi-camera one). The loss policy stays.
chains.spineLimitTooltip:
The largest rotation the spine takes away from the neutral torso, degrees (the lean and the turn of the shoulder line).
Every bone from the spine to the neck takes the same rotation.
180 changes nothing, zero keeps the torso upright.
chains.torsoDirectLossNote: When its tracking is lost, the solver holds the torso for up to half a second.
chains.torsoDirectNote: The direct pipeline carries the measured lean from the spine to the neck.
chains.torsoPositionNote: A multi-camera project measures no torso, so this chain stays at the avatar's rest. The root follows the measured shoulders instead (see Placement).
chains.wristLimitTooltip:
The largest rotation the hand takes against the forearm, degrees (the palm in the forearm's frame).
A larger bend is clamped onto its own axis at this angle.
180 changes nothing, zero holds the avatar's rest wrist. The forearm's roll is not limited.

faceTab.assignNone: Every library profile is already assigned
faceTab.autoReadOnlyText: Auto is generated from the avatar and is read-only. Duplicate it to edit a copy.
faceTab.deletePromptFmt: Delete the face profile %s? Its file is removed from the library. An avatar that uses it lists it as missing and runs Auto.
faceTab.error.invalidVariableName: '%s' is not a valid variable name
faceTab.errorsTextFmt: %d functions do not compile. The last good version keeps running.
faceTab.missingActiveText: The active profile is not in the library. Auto is running.
faceTab.missingTextFmt: Assigned profile %s is not in the library
faceTab.problem.noExpression: the avatar has no expression named '%s'
faceTab.problem.noMesh: the avatar has no mesh named '%s'
faceTab.problem.noMorph: the avatar has no morph target named '%s'

exprEditor.revertTooltip: Restore the text this row had when the editor opened on it
exprEditor.compilesText: Compiles. Edits apply live; the last good version keeps running while one does not compile.
exprEditor.traceNote: The result and what it reads. Click a name to hide its line.
exprEditor.soloOnNote: Rest face plus this row's target alone
exprEditor.soloOffNote: The whole profile, as the 3D scene shows it
exprEditor.noAvatarText: Load an avatar to preview the face.
exprEditor.fn.clamp: x held between lo and hi.
exprEditor.fn.pow: x raised to y. Bends a 0..1 input: y above 1 eases in, below 1 eases out.
exprEditor.fn.lerp: Between a and b by t: a at t = 0, b at t = 1.
exprEditor.fn.remap: x from the range inLo..inHi onto outLo..outHi (0..1 when left out), clamped to the input range.
exprEditor.fn.smoothstep: 0 below edge0, 1 above edge1, an S curve between.
exprEditor.fn.select: a when c is true (above 0.5), else b.
exprEditor.fn.hysteresis: Stateful switch: turns on when x rises above on, off when it falls below off.
exprEditor.fn.smooth: Stateful low-pass: x eased with time constant tauSeconds.
exprEditor.op.not: 1 when the value is false (0.5 or less), else 0

exprField.fallbackTooltip: The function does not compile, so the fixed value is used.
exprField.fxOffTooltip: Use a function instead of a fixed value
exprField.fxOnTooltip: Use the fixed value. The function's text is kept.
exprField.helpText: A function in the face expression language, over these inputs:
exprField.noValueTooltip: The shown frame did not evaluate this setting.
exprField.rawTooltip: The function's value before it is clamped to the setting's range.

audioPanel.enableTooltip:
Feed the microphone's visemes to the avatar's face.
The face profile decides what each source drives. The built-in Auto profile gives the phone the mouth while it sees a face.
audioPanel.gateTooltip:
Level under which the mouth rests and no analysis runs. The mouth opens fully 20 dB above it.
Set it just above the room's noise floor.
audioPanel.gainTooltip: Applied to the microphone before the gate and the analysis.
audioPanel.modelTooltip: Simple Loudness opens the mouth by level alone. MFCC classifies vowels against your calibrated profile, the uLipSync way. Oculus LipSync runs Meta's engine when its SDK is installed.
audioPanel.smoothingTooltip: How long the mouth takes to settle on a new frame, kept per model. 0 passes every frame through as it comes.
audioPanel.engineSmoothingTooltip: The Oculus engine's own viseme smoothing: 1 is its raw prediction, 100 its smoothest response.
audioPanel.profileNone: Profile: none, volume only until you calibrate
audioPanel.calibrateTooltip: Teach the vowels to your voice: five held vowels and the room's silence, three seconds each.
audioPanel.importTooltip: Load a uLipSync profile, the JSON uLipSync or VTube Studio exports.
audioPanel.weightsNone: Viseme weights: no fresh microphone sample

audioWizard.intro: This teaches the vowels to your voice and microphone, the way uLipSync is calibrated. Six prompts of three seconds each: five held vowels, then the room's silence. Each starts with a countdown.
audioWizard.introSetup: Speak at the distance and volume you will use, with the microphone where it will stay. The profile is written beside the project as a uLipSync profile and read from there.
audioWizard.deviceNotOpen: No microphone is open. Enable the microphone mouth in the Microphone stage and pick a device first.
audioWizard.promptsIntro: Hold each vowel steadily until the bar fills, then the room's silence.
audioWizard.holdFmt: After the countdown, hold "%s" for three seconds.
audioWizard.holdSilence: After the countdown, stay quiet for three seconds: the loudest moment sets the gate, and the room's sound becomes the noise phoneme.
audioWizard.errorNoCapture: No audio arrived. Check the microphone in the Microphone stage and record again.
audioWizard.errorTooQuietFmt: Too little voice passed the gate (%.1f s). Hold the vowel louder or closer and record again.
audioWizard.reviewIntro: Each vowel's own voice scored against the new profile. Under about 80 percent two vowels overlap; redo them with clearer shapes.
audioWizard.reviewGateFmt: Gate: %.0f dBFS, the room's loudest quiet moment plus 6 dB

devicePanel.exposureTooltip:
Dragging this switches the camera to MANUAL exposure.
Auto-exposure in dim light extends exposure past the
frame interval and silently halves the frame rate
(30fps -> 15fps). Shorten exposure (or add light) to
get the full rate back.

trackingPanel.bodyPoseIntro: Body tracking for measured elbows, shoulders, and head pose. Opt-in per camera: the person detector only fires on a camera that sees you upright, so leave overhead cameras off.
trackingPanel.bodyPoseProportionsIntro: Body proportions. Only lengths are assumed - every direction is measured - but they set the scale of the estimates, so correcting them for your own body is worth a minute.
trackingPanel.bodyBackendTooltip:
RTMPose body: 17 keypoints in the image, the lighter model; the
stereo rig's depth comes from the triangulated wrists.
RTMW3D whole body: 133 keypoints each with a depth relative to
the hips, the single-camera direct mode's model, several times
the cost per frame.
trackingPanel.calibrateHandsTooltip:
Guided flow: measure your bone lengths from stereo triangulation,
then capture your rest pose - in that order, enforced, because
saving bones moves the thumb's angle zero and a rest pose captured
first would be measured against a zero that no longer exists.
trackingPanel.calibrateMountingTooltip:
Opens a guided calibration: twist your forearms (which measures
each arm's long axis), then curl at the elbows (which measures
the roll about that axis, and your forearm length).
trackingPanel.captureTimingTooltip:
Where each camera's frame time goes, step by step, ~1s average.
Queue age is how long a frame waited for the vision thread; the
rows below it are what the thread then spent on that frame.
One thread serves every camera, so a slow step on one camera
delays all of them. The diagnostic dump (F9) records the raw
per-frame series.
trackingPanel.clearHandCalibrationTooltip:
Reverts to the landmark model's proportions and the flat-hand
zero, and re-enables the stereo auto hand-scale.
trackingPanel.deriveUpperArmTooltip:
Take the upper arm as a multiple of the shoulder width instead of
measuring it. Measuring it needs the arm straight and square to the
camera, which is hard to hold at a desk and reads 20%% short when
missed - and a short upper arm makes the elbow bend the wrong way.
Proportions are stable enough that a multiple of a width that IS
easy to measure wins.
trackingPanel.directCaptureTooltip:
Sit square facing the screen. A 3 second countdown runs, then the
pose is captured as the neutral the torso and head are measured
against. The hands need no capture.
trackingPanel.directEnabledTooltip:
While on, this camera's landmarks drive the avatar directly
and the fused stereo path is bypassed.
trackingPanel.directHandsNote: Direct mode measures no hand bones and needs no finger zero.
trackingPanel.directIntro: One camera, no world calibration: the avatar's own bone lengths set the scale and the camera is the world.
trackingPanel.directTiltTooltip:
The camera's downward pitch, positive looking down: 10 for a webcam
on top of the monitor, 0 at eye level, negative below the screen.
Nothing measures it; set it by hand.
trackingPanel.dumpTrackingStateDelayedTooltip:
Three seconds to get into the pose, then the same dump. In
direct mode a dump also saves the posed avatar: its skeleton
over the camera frame, the avatar rendered from the camera
beside the frame, and the solver's state behind the pose.
trackingPanel.dumpTrackingStateTooltip:
Writes the last few seconds of tracking/fusion history
(including cluster + side-assignment scores), the live config,
each camera's current frame (raw + annotated PNG) and the
frame as a one-frame recording to a timestamped folder - hit
it the moment tracking misbehaves.
trackingPanel.enableFaceTooltip:
Receives ARKit face blendshapes and head rotation from the
iFacialMocap iPhone app over UDP. The app is asked to stream
to this machine automatically. The blendshapes stream over VMC
as the avatar's expressions, and the phone's head rotation
replaces the camera head while the stream is live.
trackingPanel.enableWristImuTooltip:
Wrist-strapped inertial trackers supply FOREARM orientation at
~200 Hz, immune to occlusion. A wrist strap sits proximal to the
wrist joint, so it measures the forearm - not the palm - which is
what makes the wrist joint angle measurable and places the
elbow. The forearm drives the streamed lower arm bone.
trackingPanel.faceAlignHeadTooltip:
Look straight ahead and press: the phone's head rotation is
aligned to the camera head at the next frame both measure.
Needs the body-pose stage tracking the head. Unaligned, looking
straight at the phone faces the avatar forward.
trackingPanel.webcamFaceNone: No fresh frame from the direct camera's body model
trackingPanel.webcamFaceLost: Face not tracked (hidden, turned away or too small)
trackingPanel.webcamFaceNeutralMissing:
No face in the neutral capture: the values read against generic defaults.
Capture the neutral again with your face in view.
trackingPanel.blinkSyncEyesTooltip: Both eyes read their mean, so no wink passes.
trackingPanel.blinkWinkThresholdTooltip: How far apart the eyes must close for each to read on its own. Under it both eyes follow the less closed one.
trackingPanel.blinkClarityTooltip: How strongly a partial closure is pushed toward open or shut.
trackingPanel.blinkSensitivityTooltip: How small and slow a drop in eye openness may be and still start a blink. Higher catches more blinks and more false ones.
trackingPanel.blinkSettling: The open baselines are still learning from the first open frames.
trackingPanel.faceHeadNotAligned: Head not aligned (looking at the phone faces forward)
trackingPanel.faceNotBound: UDP port could not be bound
trackingPanel.facePhoneAddressTooltip:
Where the streaming request is sent. The default broadcast
address reaches a phone anywhere on the LAN. Enter the phone's
IP address to target it directly.
trackingPanel.facePortTooltip: The UDP port the app streams to. iFacialMocap uses 49983.
trackingPanel.flickerTooltip:
Frame-to-frame brightness oscillation of the whole image.
A steady frequency = light PWM/mains flicker beating against
the shutter (change lights, or match the shutter to the mains
rate). Oscillation with no clear frequency = auto-exposure
hunting - lock exposure and gain.
trackingPanel.flipHandednessTooltip:
MediaPipe assumes a mirrored selfie view.
Enable for a normal (non-mirrored) camera.
trackingPanel.forearmLengthTooltip:
Wrist-to-elbow distance, used to place the elbow back along the
MEASURED forearm direction. An error here slides the elbow along
the forearm axis without rotating it.

The mounting wizard's curl stage measures this from the arc the
controller sweeps, and overwrites this value. That reads slightly
SHORT of a true elbow-to-wrist length, because it is the radius to
the controller rather than to the wrist - nudge it up if the elbow
marker sits inside your actual elbow in the camera view.
trackingPanel.frameLoopHitchesTooltip:
Loop iterations over 50 ms. Every camera shares this thread, so a
hitch drops frames on ALL of them at once and shows up as a
synchronized tracking gap. The named phase is where the time
went; the log line carries the full breakdown.
trackingPanel.fusionDiagnosticsNone: No hand was fused on this frame.
trackingPanel.handCalibrationStatusFmt: Bones  L: %s  R: %s   Rest pose  L: %s  R: %s
trackingPanel.handSlotDrawModeTooltip:
How a hand slot the direct solver rejected is drawn. A slot the
body model's wrist disagrees with (the palm detector on something
hand-shaped in the scene) is hidden, dimmed, or drawn at full strength.
trackingPanel.headWidthTooltip: Ear to ear. Sets the head's distance from the camera.
trackingPanel.highlightClipTooltip:
Blown-out pixels in the hand region. Clipping erases the skin
texture and joint boundaries the landmark model reads - reduce
exposure, or diffuse/angle the light to kill specular hot spots.
trackingPanel.holdStillCountdownFmt: Get ready - hold both hands still... %d
trackingPanel.holdStillJitterTestTooltip:
Hold both hands still for a few seconds and get ONE number
per hand: the mean per-landmark deviation over the window.
With the hands genuinely still, that deviation IS tracking
noise - so run it once per camera-settings or lighting
change and compare. Uses the fused world-space output
(what clients actually receive).
trackingPanel.imageQualityHeader: Worst tracked hand per camera, ~1s average
trackingPanel.imageQualityTooltip:
Diagnoses WHY tracking jitters, in terms of the knobs that fix
it: exposure, gain, lighting, background. Statistics come from
each hand's region in the exact image the model consumed,
at a fixed working scale so values are comparable across
resolutions. Hover a metric name for what to adjust. The
diagnostic dump (F9) records the raw per-frame series.
trackingPanel.luminanceTooltip:
Mean brightness of the hand region, 0-255.
Low = underexposed: raise exposure or add light.
High = overexposed: lower exposure before highlights clip.
trackingPanel.measureMyBodyTooltip:
Measures these four lengths against your own body, using the fused
wrists as the ruler.

They are NOT anatomical numbers: they are distances between the
pose model's landmarks, which sit inside your real joints by an
amount that differs per person and per model. A guessed shoulder
width put a measured shoulder 0.8 m too far away.
trackingPanel.measuredScaleTooltip:
Your wrist->knuckle bone length, measured continuously from
stereo triangulation / depth. Nothing to configure.
trackingPanel.noiseTooltip:
Sensor noise (median-filter residual). High = auto-exposure has
cranked the gain in dim light, which directly destabilizes the
landmarks - add light so the gain comes back down.
trackingPanel.noseForwardTooltip: Ear midpoint to nose tip. Sets head yaw and pitch.
trackingPanel.separationTooltip:
Hand brightness vs the surrounding background. Low = the hand
blends in, which starves palm DETECTION (internal contrast can
still be fine). Change the surface under your hands, or light
the hands rather than the table.
trackingPanel.shadowClipTooltip:
Pixels stuck at black in the hand region. Some background is
normal; a high value together with low luminance means real
underexposure.
trackingPanel.sharpnessTooltip:
Edge strength with sensor noise filtered out first. Low = motion
blur or defocus - shorten the exposure time (adding light to
compensate) or refocus the camera.
trackingPanel.shoulderWidthTooltip: Between the shoulder joints. Sets the shoulders' distance from the camera.
trackingPanel.showBodyLandmarksTooltip:
Draws the raw body skeleton on cameras running body pose.
Landmarks below the solver's visibility gate are hidden or dimmed
(Show low-visibility landmarks), and the joints it consumes
(shoulders, elbows, wrists) carry their visibility - so a bad elbow can be traced to its source landmark.
trackingPanel.showLowVisibilityLandmarksTooltip:
Draws the body and body model landmarks below the visibility
gate, dimmed. Off, they are hidden: the model places an unseen
landmark anywhere, so it jumps around the frame.
trackingPanel.showPerCameraSkeletonsTooltip:
Draws each camera's unfused skeleton dimmed in that camera's
color - use to verify the cameras agree in world space
(they should overlap within a few cm)
trackingPanel.showWholeBodyFaceTooltip:
Draws the 68 face landmarks of the whole-body model on cameras
running it, joined along the jaw, brows, nose, eyes and lips.
Points below the visibility gate are hidden or dimmed
(Show low-visibility landmarks).
trackingPanel.showWholeBodyHandsTooltip:
Draws the whole-body model's own 21 landmarks per hand, in
orange, apart from the hand slots. Each hand belongs to the arm
the model attached it to. Points below the visibility gate are
hidden or dimmed (Show low-visibility landmarks).
trackingPanel.swapWristsTooltip: If the Joy-Con L is strapped to your RIGHT wrist
trackingPanel.timingBodyPoseTooltip: The opt-in body-pose models. Zero on cameras without the stage.
trackingPanel.timingCallbackCopyTooltip:
Time the camera driver's callback spends copying each frame out
of the driver buffer. The driver thread is blocked for this long.
trackingPanel.timingConvertTooltip:
Converting the driver's frame format (NV12, YUY2, RGB24) to BGR
on the CPU.
trackingPanel.timingDroppedFramesTooltip:
Frames the callback discarded because every buffer was still
waiting for the vision thread. Cumulative since the camera opened.
trackingPanel.timingHandInferenceTooltip:
The palm detector and hand landmark models, as the pipeline
reports it.
trackingPanel.timingLiftTooltip: Lifting the 2D landmarks into camera space and then world space.
trackingPanel.timingPublishTooltip: Copying the frame for the Stage View's camera view.
trackingPanel.timingQueueAgeTooltip:
Time from the capture callback stamping the frame to the vision
thread popping it. Grows when the thread falls behind the camera.
trackingPanel.timingQueuedFramesTooltip:
Frames waiting for the vision thread right now. More than one
means the thread is behind.
trackingPanel.timingTotalTooltip:
The whole per-camera step, from pop to publish. The difference
from the rows above is bookkeeping (seeding, recording taps).
trackingPanel.timingUndistortTooltip:
Applying the calibrated lens correction to the full frame on the
CPU. Zero until the camera has intrinsics.
trackingPanel.upperArmRatioTooltip:
NOT the anatomical ratio: the model's shoulder points sit inside
your real joints (measured at ~0.74 of a biacromial breadth), so
the familiar 'arm is about 1.5 shoulder widths' becomes ~2.0 of
THIS width, and the upper arm alone lands near 1.05.
trackingPanel.upperArmTooltip: Shoulder to elbow. Decides which of the two elbow solutions is real.
trackingPanel.wristRollErrorTooltip:
Mounting roll error, read straight off anatomy: the wrist
cannot rotate about the forearm's long axis, so any twist
measured in the wrist joint is calibration error.
Near 0 = good. A large value rolls the forearm frame, which
makes the elbow bend along a rotated arc and shows up as
phantom wrist bend when you pronate.
Recalibrate the mounting if this stays large.

oscPanel.dropoutHoldTooltip:
After a hand goes untracked (or below min confidence), keep
streaming its last good pose for this long before what follows
the hold (Then) applies. Bridges brief 2-10 frame losses so the
avatar doesn't stall and snap back. 0 = apply it immediately.
oscPanel.headOffsetTooltip:
Neck -> head bone offset. A VMC receiver replaces the position
of every bone it is sent, and nothing here measures a neck, so
this is the knob: raise it if the head sinks into the shoulders,
lower it if it floats.
oscPanel.minConfidenceTooltip:
Below this fused confidence a hand is treated as lost: after
the dropout hold its bones freeze or stop
instead of following jitter. The hold and what follows it are
on each arm chain under the Retarget stage. 0 = always send.
Watch each hand's confidence in this stage's diagnostics to
pick a threshold.
oscPanel.mouthFromBoth: from the ARKit face and the microphone's visemes
oscPanel.mouthFromNone: no source they read is live
oscPanel.portTooltip: 39539 is VMC's conventional Performer -> Marionette port.
oscPanel.readoutInfo:
Solver measurements below: palm +X
fingers, +Z out of palm, angles in degrees
oscPanel.streamStopped: Not sending: the stream is off or its socket is closed
oscPanel.vmcAvatarBoneLengths:
The avatar takes the measured
bone lengths (Body solver stage settings)
oscPanel.vmcBonesInfo:
Bones: head, clavicles, arms,
hands, fingers (39)
oscPanel.wristBendTooltip:
Rotation of the palm relative to the forearm, measured from
your mounting-calibration pose. Hold your wrist STRAIGHT: if
this doesn't drop near zero, recalibrate the mounting (or the
IMU yaw has drifted since you did).

calibrationPanel.extrinsicsAllDescription: Extrinsics are calibrated for ALL cameras in one session against the same marker placement - that shared marker defines the common world space fusion happens in. If the marker ever moves, recalibrate here.

videoPreviewPanel.noVideoStreamText: No video stream - select a camera in the Pipeline's Capture stage

timelinePanel.handBonesTooltip:
Off = fall back to the landmark model's own proportions, which is
the A/B for a bone calibration. No effect on a recording made
before one was measured.
timelinePanel.loadButtonTooltip:
Loads the recording, re-runs the full tracking pipeline on its
inputs and verifies every frame's checksum against what live
produced. Divergent frames indicate a build mismatch (recordings
verify bit-exactly only against the binary that made them).
timelinePanel.rawFramesPendingWarning: Raw frames WILL be written next recording
timelinePanel.recordRawFramesTooltip:
PRIVACY: this writes the actual camera images to disk as JPEGs,
next to the recording. Off by default, and worth leaving off
unless you are chasing a problem.

What it buys: a landmark recording cannot answer whether a
different pose model would have done better, because the model's
input is gone. With frames, that becomes an offline measurement
(--replay-bodypose) instead of a live impression.

Costs roughly 3-6 MB per second per camera.
timelinePanel.resimulateTooltip:
Re-runs the whole recording with these parameters. The original
recorded output is untouched - flip the view radio (or compare
the deltas below) to judge a candidate fix against the incident.
timelinePanel.showReplayTooltip:
Feeds the 3D scene from the replay at the scrub position
instead of live tracking. Live tracking and OSC keep running
either way.
timelinePanel.startRecordingTooltip:
Captures every input to the tracking stages (per-camera
landmarks, depth samples, timestamps) so the whole pipeline can
be re-run offline bit-exactly. Starting RESETS the transient
tracking state (brief blip), and editing any tracking/fusion
setting while recording finalizes the file. Roughly 0.5-1 MB
per second.
timelinePanel.viewModeTooltip: Which output the 3D scene shows at the scrub position

intrinsicsWizard.boardInstructionsFmt: Calibrate the camera lens using a printed charuco board. Print the board at 100%% scale, measure a square to confirm its size, then capture it from 12 different angles/positions. TILT MATTERS: focal length can only be measured from perspective, so several captures must have the board clearly angled toward/away from the camera - flat-on captures alone cannot calibrate. Also cover the frame edges for distortion.
intrinsicsWizard.boardTooSmallError: Board must be at least 3x3 squares
intrinsicsWizard.calibrationDidNotConvergeError: Camera calibration solve did not converge - try recapturing with better board coverage
intrinsicsWizard.exportBoardButton: Export + open board PNG for printing...
intrinsicsWizard.exportBoardTooltip:
Writes the board to resources/calibration and opens it in your image
viewer. Print at 100%% scale and check a square with a ruler - a
rescaled print silently rescales the whole tracking world. The same
board is the extrinsics target, so its FORWARD label sets the world
axes.
intrinsicsWizard.showBoardHint: Show the board / move it to a new position
intrinsicsWizard.squareLargerThanMarkerError: Square size must be larger than marker size
intrinsicsWizard.testUndistortExplanation: The Stage View now shows the undistorted image. Straight lines in the scene should look straight.
intrinsicsWizard.tiltExplanation: Enough flat captures - the remaining samples must show real perspective, or the focal length can't be solved.
intrinsicsWizard.tiltWarning: TILT the board toward/away from the camera

extrinsicsWizard.cameraSummaryFmt: Camera %d: %.2f m from marker, height %.2f m, reproj %.2f px
extrinsicsWizard.exportMarkerButton: Export + open marker PNG for printing...
extrinsicsWizard.exportMarkerTooltip:
Writes the marker to resources/calibration and opens it in your
image viewer. Print at 100%% scale and check the square with a
ruler - a rescaled print silently rescales the whole tracking
world. The sheet also carries the axis labels this world frame
depends on.
extrinsicsWizard.handScaleSanityCheckFmt: Sanity check these numbers against your physical setup. Hand scale is measured automatically from stereo/depth while tracking runs (current: %.1f cm).
extrinsicsWizard.markerNotVisibleHint: marker not visible to this camera
extrinsicsWizard.needVideoWarning: Start video streams on all cameras first
extrinsicsWizard.needsIntrinsicsExplanation: Extrinsics are always calibrated for ALL cameras together, against the same marker placement - otherwise the cameras end up in disagreeing world frames.
extrinsicsWizard.needsIntrinsicsWarning: Every camera needs calibrated intrinsics first
extrinsicsWizard.orientationWarning: ORIENTATION MATTERS: lay the sheet down the way it reads, with the printed FORWARD arrow pointing away from you. That makes the tracking world +X forward, +Y left, +Z up.
extrinsicsWizard.pairInvalidFmt: Cameras %d+%d: not enough shared corners to validate
extrinsicsWizard.pairQualityFmt: Cameras %d+%d agree to %.2f px rms, marker size err %.2f mm, scale %.3f
extrinsicsWizard.pairQualityTooltip:
The marker corners both cameras saw, triangulated with the new
extrinsics and checked against the marker's known size. rms px is
comparable to the tracking pipeline's triangulation residual; the
size error and scale catch a wrong baseline that reprojection
alone can hide. Only four corners, so read it as pass/fail.
extrinsicsWizard.samplingStatus: Sampling marker pose on every camera...
extrinsicsWizard.verifySetupIntro: Place the printed origin aruco marker flat on the table where the world origin should be. The marker stays there during hand tracking - it defines the tracking space. ALL cameras are calibrated in this one session so they agree on the same marker placement; make sure every camera can see it.

handWizard.boneMeasurementSummaryFmt: %s: wrist->knuckle %.1f mm, %d samples, worst spread %.1f mm
handWizard.bonesCountdownHint: Get both hands into view of two cameras...
handWizard.bonesIntroFmt:
Step 1 of 2: measure your hand bones.

The landmark model's metric hand is not your hand - its proximal phalanges run about half length - which biases the single-camera depth solve and ships the wrong skeleton to clients. This samples every stereo-triangulated frame for %d seconds and takes the median of each bone.

During the window: keep BOTH hands where two cameras see them, and move them through varied poses and rotations, so no bone stays aligned with a camera's view ray.
handWizard.deskCountdownHint: Lay both hands flat on the desk beside the marker...
handWizard.deskIntroFmt:
Step 1 of 2: measure your hand bones from the desk.

With one camera the desk stands in for the second view: lay BOTH hands flat on the desk beside the marker, palms down, fingers spread and straight, where the camera sees them whole. Sampling runs for %d seconds, measures each bone from the desk plane, and measures how deep this camera reads a hand.
handWizard.deskLiftScaleMissingFmt: %s camera depth scale not measured (%d samples)
handWizard.deskRestCountdownHint: Hold your rest pose where the camera sees both hands...
handWizard.deskRestIntro:
Step 2 of 2: capture your rest pose.

This pose becomes the all-zero-angles reference, captured now, after the bone save, because measured bones move the thumb's angle zero.

Hold both hands relaxed where the camera sees them, as they will rest while tracking.
handWizard.deskSamplingHint: Sampling - keep both hands flat and still
handWizard.leftOnlyCaptured: Captured left hand only - the right hand was not stereo-tracked
handWizard.nothingCaptured: Nothing captured - both hands need two cameras on them
handWizard.restIntro:
Step 2 of 2: capture your rest pose.

This pose becomes the all-zero-angles reference. Without it, zero means an idealized flat hand, and a hand hovering over a keyboard genuinely holds tens of degrees of knuckle flexion.

It is captured NOW, after the bone save, on purpose: measured bones move the thumb's angle zero, so a rest pose captured before them would be measured against a zero that no longer exists.

Hold both hands in your rest pose - flat, fingers together and straight - where two cameras see them.
handWizard.rightOnlyCaptured: Captured right hand only - the left hand was not stereo-tracked

bodyWizard.calibrationMissingStatus: That camera needs intrinsics AND extrinsics first
bodyWizard.cameraEnabledStatus: Body pose enabled on a camera
bodyWizard.cameraNotEnabledStatus: No camera has body pose enabled
bodyWizard.frontalExplainLine1: A raised hand puts a measured wrist at about the distance your
bodyWizard.frontalExplainLine2: torso is from the camera, and that is all the shoulders and ears
bodyWizard.frontalExplainLine3: need in order to be measured. Nothing has to be straight: the
bodyWizard.frontalExplainLine4: upper arm is worked out from your shoulder width instead, because
bodyWizard.frontalExplainLine5: measuring it directly needed a pose that was too hard to hold.
bodyWizard.frontalOneHandEnoughInstructions: ONE HAND IS ENOUGH, and either will do - hold one up, let it count, and you are done. The other can stay on the desk.
bodyWizard.frontalRaiseHandInstructions: Face the camera and simply RAISE ONE HAND up beside your shoulder, as though waving. Keep it near your shoulder rather than reaching out.
bodyWizard.fusedWristsNoteLine1: The fused wrists are the ruler: they are the only metric,
bodyWizard.fusedWristsNoteLine2: world-anchored points, measured by the other cameras.
bodyWizard.handOffsetFmt: %.0f%% of a shoulder width away (needs under %.0f%%)
bodyWizard.headTurnExplainLine1: Facing the camera, your nose sits on top of the midpoint between
bodyWizard.headTurnExplainLine2: your ears and says nothing about how far it juts forward. Turning
bodyWizard.headTurnExplainLine3: swings that offset across the image, where it can be measured.
bodyWizard.headTurnInstructions: Now keep your body still and slowly turn your head to look left, then right, as though checking both ends of your desk.
bodyWizard.headTurnSamplesNotAcceptedFmt: %d samples - turn further, the head still reads face-on
bodyWizard.leftNotTracked: Left hand: not counting - not tracked
bodyWizard.leftTooFar: Left hand: not counting - too far from your shoulder, raise it
bodyWizard.notEnoughSamplesExplain: Every sample needs both hands tracked, the shoulders, elbows and ears visible, and the arms held across the camera rather than toward it.
bodyWizard.rightNotTracked: Right hand: not counting - not tracked
bodyWizard.rightTooFar: Right hand: not counting - too far from your shoulder, raise it
bodyWizard.sampleSpreadFmt: Sample spread %.0f%% - hold stiller for a cleaner result.
bodyWizard.upperArmNoteLine1Fmt: The upper arm is not measured: it is taken as %.2f x the shoulder
bodyWizard.upperArmNoteLine2: width, which only needs a width that is easy to measure. Measuring
bodyWizard.upperArmNoteLine3: it directly needed the arm straight and square to the camera, and
bodyWizard.upperArmNoteLine4Fmt: a missed pose read it 20%% short - enough to bend the elbow wrongly.
bodyWizard.verifyIntro: Measures the body lengths the elbow, shoulder and head estimates rest on. These are not anatomical numbers: they are distances between the pose model's own landmarks, which sit inside your real joints by an amount that differs per person and per model, so they have to be measured rather than assumed.

mountingWizard.biasStep1Explain: A gyro reads a small nonzero rate even when perfectly still, and that offset integrates into drift. Sitting still is the one situation where the true rate is known to be zero, so the reading IS the error - including about the vertical axis, which nothing else in the system can measure.
mountingWizard.biasStep1Intro: Step 1 of 3: REST. Take the controllers off and lay them flat on the desk. Do not touch them until this finishes.
mountingWizard.calibratedFmt: Calibrated (arm axis %.2f, hinge %.0f deg off it)
mountingWizard.curlElbowHint: keep the shoulder still - bend at the elbow only
mountingWizard.curlPurpose: The elbow hinge points across the forearm, so this second direction of rotation is what fixes the roll that a twist alone cannot see. It also measures the distance from your elbow to the controller.
mountingWizard.curlStep3Intro: Step 3 of 3: CURL. Keep your PALMS FACING DOWN and your upper arms still, then raise and lower each hand at the elbow, several times - a slow bicep curl. Do not twist your forearms during this.
mountingWizard.curlVisibility: KEEP BOTH HANDS VISIBLE to the cameras. The cameras decide only which way round your palm faces, so a rough view is enough.
mountingWizard.filterDivergedFmt:
%s: this controller's orientation filter has diverged.
  Set it down, redo the rest step, and try again.
mountingWizard.handNotVisibleFmt: %s: hand not visible - the cameras must see it
mountingWizard.moveBackOtherWayFmt: %s: move back the other way too
mountingWizard.notCaptured: Not captured - the controller stopped streaming
mountingWizard.putControllersBack: Put the controllers back on your wrists.
mountingWizard.reasonCurlSmall:
Rejected - the CURL was too small - raise and lower your hand
  further, several times.
  Nothing was saved for this side.
mountingWizard.reasonGeneric:
Rejected - the motions were not good enough.
  Nothing was saved for this side.
mountingWizard.reasonHandDirectionUnclear:
Rejected - the curl did not show which way the hand points -
  bend at the elbow rather than moving the whole arm.
  Nothing was saved for this side.
mountingWizard.reasonPalmUnknown:
Rejected - the cameras never saw the hand, so which way the
  palm faces is unknown.
  Nothing was saved for this side.
mountingWizard.reasonSameAxis:
Rejected - the curl turned about the same axis as the twist -
  keep the shoulder still and bend only at the elbow.
  Nothing was saved for this side.
mountingWizard.reasonStrokesDisagreed:
Rejected - the curl strokes disagreed - keep the palms facing
  down and do not twist while curling.
  Nothing was saved for this side.
mountingWizard.reasonTwistWeak:
Rejected - the TWIST did not pin the forearm axis - rotate
  further, and back the other way too.
  Nothing was saved for this side.
mountingWizard.reviewCheckIntro: Keep your hands straight in line with your forearms. The wrist bend below should read near zero, and should stay near zero as you twist your forearms. If it climbs while you twist, the mounting is still wrong.
mountingWizard.skipBiasTooltip:
The mounting calibration still works; yaw will just drift
faster and lean harder on the camera to correct it.
mountingWizard.twistElbowHint: keep the elbow still - twist only
mountingWizard.twistNote: Turning one way only does not count, and neither does waving your arms around - the bar needs back-and-forth rotation about the forearm itself.
mountingWizard.twistPurpose: This finds the forearm's long axis, which is what places the elbow.
mountingWizard.twistStep2Intro: Step 2 of 3: TWIST. Hold your forearms roughly HORIZONTAL and rotate each one as if slowly turning a doorknob - palm up, palm down, and back again, several times. Keep your elbows still; it is the twist that is measured.
mountingWizard.verifyIntro: This measures how each controller is strapped to your wrist, so the app can turn a sensor orientation into a FOREARM orientation. Two motions supply it: a twist of the forearms, then a curl at the elbows.
mountingWizard.verifyStrapInstructions: Strap each controller to the top of the wrist, pointing along the forearm. The exact orientation does not matter - that is what this calibration absorbs - but it must not shift afterwards.
mountingWizard.waitingForController: Waiting for at least one controller to stream and settle

pipeline.descCapture: Per-camera frames and the models that run on them: video capture and undistortion, the hand models, the optional body model, and the lift into camera and world space.
pipeline.descCamera: One camera's device, video mode and calibration, and the per-camera stages that run on its frames.
pipeline.descVideo: Frame capture, conversion to BGR, undistortion with the camera's intrinsics, and the luminance flicker check.
pipeline.descHandModels: Palm detection and hand landmarks on this camera's frame, producing 2D landmarks per hand slot.
pipeline.descBodyModel: Person detection and the body landmark model on this camera, on its own frame divider.
pipeline.descLift: 2D landmarks lifted to camera space, then moved to world space when the camera has extrinsics.
pipeline.descFusion: Clusters every camera's world-space hands into one hand per side, triangulates where two cameras agree, and runs the hand state estimator.
pipeline.descImu: Wrist-strapped controller orientation, filtered and anchored to the fused palm's yaw, giving the forearm orientation.
pipeline.descBodySolver: Places the shoulders, elbows and head in the world from the body camera's 2D landmarks, the calibrated lengths and the fused wrists.
pipeline.descDirectSolver: Solves the torso, head and arm chains from one camera's landmark rays with no world calibration. Stands in for Fusion, IMU and Body solver.
pipeline.descFilters: Filtering of pixels and depths, landmark visibility gates, and the entry gate for an arm coming from rest.
pipeline.descTorso: Shoulder depth from the known shoulder width, the lean from the neutral capture, and the head from the ears and nose or the phone.
pipeline.descArmChain: The wrist's distance along its ray, scored over the reachable interval, with the elbow on the bone circle.
pipeline.descPalm: The camera-space palm with its depth mirror resolved by the forearm, and finger angles against each finger's metacarpal.
pipeline.descHoldRest: Each group holds its last solution for the hold it has earned, then eases to the rig's rest pose.
pipeline.descSourcePose: The hand-off both pipelines share: a humanoid skeleton in the user's proportions with per-bone confidence, which of position, direction and roll were measured, and the finger angles.
pipeline.descRetarget: Maps the source pose onto the avatar's skeleton and applies the loss policy.
pipeline.descOutput: Turns the avatar pose into VMC bones and face values and sends them over UDP.
pipeline.descDeliveryRules: The confidence threshold and the send rate. VMC has no tracked flag, so validity is expressed through which bones arrive.
pipeline.descVmcStream: The encoded OSC bundles: bones, blend values, the avatar announcement, and the target address.
pipeline.descFace: The phone face stream and the microphone visemes, evaluated through the avatar's active face profile.
pipeline.descPhone: The iFacialMocap UDP stream: the ARKit blendshapes and the head rotation.
pipeline.descWebcam: The direct camera's whole-body face points as ARKit columns: the jaw, the smile, the pucker, the brows and the blinks.
pipeline.descBlink: The webcam's eye openness turned into blinks over time: a fast drop under each eye's open baseline starts a blink, a slow sag moves the baseline. Read by profiles as blink.*.
pipeline.descMicrophone: Audio capture and the mouth model that turns it into visemes.
pipeline.descProfile: The active face profile's expressions evaluated over the phone and microphone sources into expression and morph target values.
pipeline.whyNoDeviceFmt: Camera %.0f has no device open. Pick one in this camera's stage under Capture.
pipeline.whyCameraNoIntrinsicsFmt: Camera %.0f has no intrinsics, so its hands stay 2D. Run the intrinsics calibration.
pipeline.whyNoExtrinsicsAll: No camera has extrinsics, so nothing is lifted to world space. Run the extrinsics calibration.
pipeline.whyNoSuchCamera: The project has no such camera.
pipeline.whyTrackingPaused: A calibration wizard has paused tracking on this camera.
pipeline.whyNoIntrinsicsVideo: The camera has no intrinsics, so frames are not undistorted.
pipeline.whyCameraNotRunning: The camera is not delivering frames.
pipeline.whyHandPipelineFailed: The hand models failed to start on this camera. See the log.
pipeline.whyBodyDisabled: Body pose is not enabled on this camera.
pipeline.whyBodyModelMissing: Body pose is enabled, but its models did not load. Check the models folder.
pipeline.whyNoIntrinsicsLift: Without intrinsics the landmarks cannot be lifted to 3D.
pipeline.whyDirectNoWorld: Direct mode has no world calibration. The camera is the world.
pipeline.whyNoExtrinsicsLift: This camera has no extrinsics, so its hands stay in camera space. Run the extrinsics calibration.
pipeline.whyFusionPassthrough: No camera has a world pose, so camera 1's camera-space result passes through unchanged and no hand is streamed. Run the extrinsics calibration.
pipeline.whyNoCameraFrames: No camera has produced a frame.
pipeline.whyImuDisabled: The wrist IMU is not enabled in this project.
pipeline.whyImuNotConnected: The wrist IMU is enabled and no controller is connected. Close other apps that hold the controllers if they fail to open.
pipeline.whyImuOneMissing: Only one of the two wrist controllers is connected.
pipeline.whyImuNotCalibrated: A wrist controller has no mounting calibration. Run the mounting calibration.
pipeline.whyImuReplay: The IMU filter is not replayed. A recording carries the forearm it produced.
pipeline.whyNotRecorded: This take holds no stage state for this frame. It was recorded before stage state was kept.
pipeline.whyImuNoYawAnchor: The filter anchors its yaw to the fused palm, which needs a world pose.
pipeline.whyImuSilent: A wrist controller is connected and has stopped sending samples.
pipeline.whyImuConverging: A wrist controller's orientation filter has not settled yet.
pipeline.whyNoBodyCamera: No camera in this project runs the body model.
pipeline.whyBodyNeedsWorld: The body solve is anchored to world-space wrists, and there are none without extrinsics.
pipeline.whyBodyCameraUncalibratedFmt: The body camera, camera %.0f, needs intrinsics and extrinsics.
pipeline.whyBodyImuForearms: The wrist IMUs supply the forearms. This solver supplies the shoulders and the head.
pipeline.whyDirectNoIntrinsics: The direct camera has no intrinsics. Run the intrinsics calibration.
pipeline.whyDirectNoAvatar: Direct mode poses the avatar's own skeleton, so it needs an avatar loaded.
pipeline.whyDirectNoNeutral: No neutral pose is captured, so the lean and the head have no zero. Capture the neutral pose.
pipeline.whyDirectHandednessSwapped: The hand tracker labels left and right the wrong way round. The body model is correcting the labels while it sees the hands, and a hand it does not see is rejected. Change Flip handedness in the tracking settings.
pipeline.whySourceNoArms: No arm is measured in world space, so there is nothing to retarget.
pipeline.whyRetargetNoAvatar: No avatar is loaded, so the measured-length skeleton is streamed as it is. Load an avatar to keep its proportions.
pipeline.whyOscSocket: The UDP socket could not be opened. See the log.
pipeline.whyOutputNoWorld: A hand needs a world-anchored palm to be streamed, so only face values go out.
pipeline.whyPhoneDisabled: The phone face stream is turned off.
pipeline.whyPhonePort: The UDP port for the phone face stream could not be bound.
pipeline.whyPhoneWaiting: Waiting for the phone app to stream.
pipeline.whyWebcamNotDirect: The webcam face reads the direct camera, so it needs a direct project.
pipeline.whyWebcamNoBody: Waiting for the direct camera's whole-body model to see a person.
pipeline.whyWebcamNeutral: The neutral capture holds no face. Capture the neutral again with the face in view.
pipeline.whyBlinkNotDirect: The blink stage reads the direct camera, so it needs a direct project.
pipeline.whyBlinkSettling: The eyes' open baselines are still learning from the first open frames.
pipeline.whyMicDisabled: The microphone mouth is turned off.
pipeline.whyMicDevice: The microphone device is not open.
pipeline.whyMicBackend: The mouth model is not available. See the stage's diagnostics.
pipeline.whyFaceOff: Neither the phone face stream nor the microphone mouth is turned on.
pipeline.whyFaceNoSource: A face source is turned on and none is delivering.
pipeline.whyProfileProblems: Some of the face profile's targets do not exist on this avatar and are skipped.

Wrist-to-elbow distance in the body model's landmark space.
The arm chain is solved with it and the upper arm, so the
elbow's reprojection fixes the wrist's distance in your
proportions. The wrist IMU mounting wizard also measures it.

sourceStage.noSource: No source pose on the shown frame.

stageInspector.nothingSelected: Nothing is selected. Select a stage in the Pipeline panel.
stageInspector.settingsElsewhere: This stage's inputs, settings and diagnostics are still in the other panels.

stageView.titleWizard: Camera view: all cameras, for the calibration wizard
stageView.modeTooltip:
What the view shows. Follow selection shows the cameras for the Capture and
Direct solver stages and the 3D scene for the others. Cameras + 3D scene shows
both side by side, with a bar between them to drag.
stageView.wizardNote:
A camera calibration wizard is running: the view shows every camera
until it closes.
stageView.povTooltip:
Where the scene is seen from. Free cam is the camera you turn by hand. A camera shows
the scene through its own lens, framed the way its video is, so the avatar's pose
compares with that camera's view of you. Direct mode places the direct camera at the
measured shoulders.
stageView.povNotCalibrated: This camera's lens is not calibrated yet.
stageView.povNoExtrinsics: This camera has no placement yet. Calibrate the extrinsics.
stageView.povNotDirectCamera: In direct mode only the direct camera has a placement, the one the solver gives it.
stageView.povNoPlacement: No placement on this frame, so the free cam is shown.
stageView.layoutTooltip:
Overlay draws the source pose over the avatar. Side by side draws
the source pose on the left and the avatar on the right, turning
together.
stageView.retargetLegend: Solid: measured. Dashed: carried over. Color: confidence, green high, amber low. Magenta cross: IK goal. Click a bone to select its chain.

performancePanel.replayNote: A replay is shown. The frame loop here is the live one.
performancePanel.sourceTooltip:
Live shows the frame loop running now. Recording shows the shown take's
frames up to the playhead, as they were recorded.
performancePanel.recordingUnavailable: Available while a replay is shown whose take recorded its stage state.
performancePanel.recordedNote: Recorded totals are the sum of the phases, and the diagnostics time is the previous frame's.
performancePanel.windowNotRecorded: No frame up to the playhead recorded its times.
